title: Comparison grid
subject: English Language
source: Seeded from english-language/y10 lessons 34, 36 (Comparison grid (pupil PDF))
intro: To understand how to compare what two writers think about the same subject

questions.q: Add one row to the grid: tone.
questions.a: A: accusing, urgent; B: warm, wondering.
questions.model: Tone = the voice. Read a line of each aloud: A is sharp and urgent; B is gentle and admiring.

questions.q: Find one similarity with evidence from both.
questions.a: Both see the sea as food: 'stops feeding us' and 'silver harvests'.

questions.q: Write your introduction in two sentences.
questions.a: Both writers value the sea; however, Text B sees an inexhaustible gift, whereas Text A sees a victim of human carelessness.
questions.model: Sentence 1: what they share. Sentence 2: the central difference, with 'whereas'.

questions.q: Plan one integrated paragraph on 'human power over the sea'.
Core: in the portal response box, write a comparative paragraph on the writers' views of the sea, using the grid. Starter: 'Both writers...; however,...'
questions.a: A paragraph with a similarity, two differences and evidence from both.
questions.model: Both writers value the sea as a source of food; however, their views of its future differ sharply. Text B's 'silver harvests' present a 'generous storehouse' that 'no labour of man could ever empty', whereas Text A warns that if we keep 'treating the sea as a bin', it will stop 'feeding us'.

questions.q: Extend: add a sentence explaining why the views differ (context).
questions.a: Text B was written before industrial fishing and plastics.

questions.q: Stretch: which writer do you find more convincing and why?
questions.a: Answers vary; strong answers weigh evidence and tone.

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, write the introduction, two integrated paragraphs and a conclusion: 'Compare how the writers present their ideas about the sea.' Starter: 'Both writers...'
questions.a: A full integrated comparison with evidence from both texts.
questions.model: Both writers value the sea, yet they see its future very differently. Text B believes humans are too small to harm it, as 'no labour of man could ever empty it', whereas Text A argues we are already doing so by 'treating the sea as a bin'. Ultimately, the difference reflects their times: one writes before industrial fishing and plastic, the other amid their consequences.

questions.q: Extend: check each paragraph names both texts.
Stretch: comment on the difference in form (letter and article).
questions.a: The private letter is reflective; the public article persuades.
Both may be right for their times; the sea has changed.
